chapter_title: Concerning the Light Mind, why it does not exercise Foreknowledge for the Saint as for the Apostle?
chapter_note: This chapter is dominated by a late Q&A setting about the elect/holy church and five practical-ethical reasons limiting foreknowledge. It lacks the impersonal, systematic cosmos→cosmos correspondential mappings that mark the oldest substrate; instead it applies doctrine to church ranks (elect/saints/apostle) and social outcomes (humility, disputes, money-making divination). No NT citation overlay appears, but the whole unit reads as community catechetical/pastoral reasoning wrapped in dialogue frame.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Hagiographic Q&A apparatus (“Once again… questioned the apostle”), with institutional referents (“holy church”, “faithful and the elect”) and argumentative opinion; not impersonal cosmological exposition.
Dialogue-attribution plus didactic answer addressed to the elect/faithful; focuses on what the elect can ‘persist in’ rather than mapping cosmic structures. ‘Apostle’ is a compilation-layer title.
Practical institutional rationale (humility, rank: “become an apostle”), framed as the first reason; no correspondential cosmology.
Second reason concerns interpersonal governance (“knowing each other’s heart”, despising, bodily shame). This is ethics/community-control, not cosmos→cosmos description.

Third reason grounds conflict in ‘flesh’ and indwelling Sin, but used to explain community disputes among elect; the language functions as moral-psychological application rather than systematic cosmology.
Fourth reason (lifespan foreknowledge affecting righteousness) is pastoral governance; fragmentary text but still oriented to behavior management within embodied life.
Fifth reason explicitly reaches into the contemporary world (magicians, fortune-tellers, taking money, travel); clear cosmos→world ‘application’ rather than substrate mapping.
Summative rationale for withholding revelation ‘from the elect’ until post-mortem; still keyed to church categories and pastoral control of disclosure rather than old systematic teaching.
Concluding promise of total unveiling after release from the body; an eschatological reassurance addressed to the elect/saints, not a structured correspondential exposition.
